## About page (`/about-us`) - SEO rewrite, heading semantics, JSON-LD
- Copy: the EN "about" strings went from **512 to 243 words** (13 keys deleted, 9 added, both locales: 357 keys each, verified equal with no per-language duplicates). Deleted: `about.video.p1/h2/p2`, `about4.p3/secB/secC/secD/a1/a2/b1/b2/c1/c2` (the `secD` block was a literal duplicate of `secC`). Kept key names `about4.title1` (now the H1 copy) / `about4.tag2` / `about4.secA`; new: `about4.w1-w4`, `about4.linkServices`, `about4.linkDoctors`, `about.video.step1-3`. No `about4.*` key is referenced anywhere outside `AboutUsInfo4.js`.
- Markup: the page's only `<h1>` is now in `AboutUsInfo4` (`<h3 class="h3-md steelblue-color">` -> `<h1>`; `PageBanner` renders **no** heading - its `<h4>` is commented out upstream). Second title -> `<h2>`, "what you get" label -> a real `<h3 class="h6">`, the 8-bullet service wall (which duplicated `Services7` and repeated a1/c1) -> 4 bullets in two `<ul>`s, the `height:150px` inline clamps are gone, and the video block is a 3-step `<ol>` (numbering comes from the markup). Eyebrows are `<p class="h4|h5 about-eyebrow">` instead of an `<h4>/<h5>` inside `span.section-id`; `<img>` -> `next/image` with descriptive alts; two real `<Link>`s to `/all-services` and `/all-doctors` (both routes exist).
- **Two CSS-specificity traps** (both fixed in `public/css/customStyle.css`, worth remembering for any future heading/list work here): (1) `style.css` sizes headings with **element-qualified** classes - `h3.h3-md` = 42px, `.txt-block h3.h3-md` = 30px margin, `p.p-sm` = 15.2px, `.steelblue-color` is scoped to `h2`-`h6` and `.section-id`/`.box-list p` are element-qualified too - so `h1.h3-md`, `.txt-block h1.h3-md`/`h2.h3-md`, `h1.steelblue-color`/`h2.steelblue-color`, `li.p-sm` and `.txt-block p.about-eyebrow` are declared explicitly. Without them the H1/H2 fell back to `#222`/grey (near-black vs the template's dark teal `#004861`), the `<li class="p-sm">` bullets inherited the container's 20px, and `.box-list p`'s 8px beat the eyebrow's 28px.
- Verified parity with the old look by computed style (desktop): H1/H2 `42px / 30px / rgb(0,72,97)`, eyebrow `24px / 28px`, bullets `15.2px`, links `20px / rgb(59,95,29)`, video H2 `42px`, steps `20px`. Mobile (390px) scales down identically because the same media queries still match.
- **Structured data**: new `src/components/Common/PageStructuredData.js` - a `pathname -> JSON-LD` registry (currently only `/about-us`: one `@graph` with `MedicalBusiness` + `BreadcrumbList`) that `pages/_app.js` renders next to `SeoMetadata`. It must live there: `_app` wraps the whole app in MUI `<NoSsr>` + `PersistGate`, so **page markup is client-rendered only** - the served HTML for `/about-us` (and every other page) is `<div id="__next">` + the Preloader (~2KB). Anything a page component puts in `<Head>` is therefore absent from the first-pass HTML; the `<script id="page-structured-data">` now appears in the SSR response (verified with `curl`: 1 script, both `@type`s, valid JSON). This also explains why there is no canonical/`og:url` unless `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is set - it is **unset** in `.env`/`.env.production`, and `NEXTAUTH_URL` uses the apex `healthpath.co.in` while `TermsPage.js` hardcodes `https://www.healthpath.co.in` (pick one before publishing absolute URLs).
- Page meta (title/description/keywords for `/about-us`) lives in the **Marketing Panel DB** (`MARKETING_PAGES.about`), set via `/marketing/seo` - nothing in the repo controls them. Suggested values (50/154/128 chars): title `About HealthPath | Online Doctor & Home Healthcare`; description `HealthPath offers online doctor consultations, clinic visits and home healthcare across India - 178+ doctors, 20+ specialities, 7 AM to 10 PM, all 7 days.`; keywords `doctor consultation online, home healthcare India, doctor home visit, nursing care at home, lab test at home, HealthPath Gurgaon`.
- Verified with `scripts/tmp-verify-about-page.mjs` (kept; needs `next dev` up): desktop 1440 / mobile 390 / HI - exactly 1 `<h1>`, H1->H2->H3 order, 0 `ul|ol|div` nested in `<p>`, 2 bullet lists (4 items), 3-step `<ol>`, both internal links resolve, JSON-LD parses, `overflow: none`, only the pre-existing MUI `findDOMNode` console warning. `npx next lint` -> 0 errors and no warnings in the touched files.
- Visually checked at 1440px and 390px (screenshots). Note the template's `wow fadeInUp` blocks start at `opacity: 0` until scrolled into view, which is why an element screenshot of `#info-1` is blank until you `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` first.
- Cross-route safety of those new rules was checked by deleting them from the CSSOM at runtime (`/`, `/all-services`): **no element on any other route matches** `h1|h2.steelblue-color`, `h1|h2.h3-md` or `li.p-sm`, while on `/about-us` dropping them regresses the H1 to 40px/`#222`, the H2 to 32px/grey and the bullets to 20px. So the rules are exactly what keeps the About page identical to its previous look, and they change nothing elsewhere.
- Still open on this page (unchanged, out of scope): the shared `Statistic1` numbers (`s7.title*`/`s4.*`), `Services7`'s legacy `s7.h4` card copy ("Healthpath: Your Convenient Path to healthier life, Open Daily" - the same string is also hardcoded in `WhoWeAreInfo9.js`) and its `#` links, `robots.txt`/`sitemap.xml` (neither exists), and the `NoSsr`/client-only rendering itself.


## `GET /api/medicineInfo` - server side paging (medicine autocomplete + `/medicine/homepage`)
- Params (mutually exclusive filters, first match wins: `alphabet` -> `medicineName` -> `search`): `alphabet=X` prefix on `name` (the A-Z tabs), `medicineName=X` prefix (prescription autocomplete, unchanged), `search=X` contains; plus `limit` (default 50, hard cap 500) and `page` (default 1). All three filters escape RegExp metacharacters - before this, `?medicineName=(` threw and answered **500**.
- Response keeps its old shape and adds paging: `{ medicines, totalCount, page, limit, totalPages }`, sorted by `name`; results are raw documents (`name`/`salt` only - `description`/`price` are rendered but **not** in `src/models/medicineInfo.js`, so those cards show blank/`₹undefined`).
- Why it matters: unfiltered the endpoint returned the whole collection - `medicineName=a` = **27,689 docs / 6.1 MB / 3.8 s**; one-letter lookups therefore overlapped, the browser aborted them and `MedicineForm` reported `TypeError: Failed to fetch` as "Failed to fetch medicines". Now `?medicineName=a&limit=50` is ~11 KB / 0.5 s; `?alphabet=Z&limit=25` = 10,243 total (410 pages); `?search=paracetamol&limit=25` = 38 total.
- Consumers (only two): `lib/MedicineForm.js` (`&limit=50`, `AbortController` + request-id guard, `response.ok` check, free-text "Add anyway" fallback) and `MedicineDeliveryComp.js` (`/medicine/homepage`: letter tab or debounced `search`, 25/page, server side). `constant.js#getAllMedicine` is unused.
- Server side paging means the A-Z tabs are now paged by the API, so a letter tab holds 410 pages instead of one in-memory array; `MedicineDeliveryComp` used to also render `router.push(...)` with no `useRouter()` import (ReferenceError on card click) - fixed while wiring the paging.

## Super-admin - "Consultation booked" page redesigned (`/superAdmin/consultationBooked`)
- Scope: `src/components/superAdminComponent/ConsultationBooked/**` + `css/ConsultationBooked.module.css`. Visual language copied from `css/Homepage.module.css` / `AddDoctor/AddDoctorForm.module.css` (brand green `#3b5f1d`, yellow `#8e8333`, 1180px page, white 14px-radius cards, 6px green left-border hero, uppercase `cardTitle`, serif figures, `primaryBtn`/`ghostBtn`, inline `note`/`noteOk`/`noteErr`, `errorBox` + `Retry`), so all three panels read as one product.
- What was replaced: the three 400x200px `.circle` filter blobs became keyboard-reachable filter tiles (`<button aria-pressed>`, active tile = green border + tinted bg + "Showing below"); the `Col md-2` heading rows became real `<table>`s (a header can no longer drift out of line with its rows); the MUI `Snackbar`/`Alert` and `window.alert` were dropped for inline notes; the status `<select>` keeps a per-row draft value and its Update button stays disabled until the value actually changes.
- **The page now loads its own data.** It used to read only `superAdminHomePage.allAppointments` / `.allDoctors`, which are filled by the *home* page, so a deep link or a hard refresh rendered an empty page. `loadBookings()` runs one `Promise.all` over `GET api.bookConsultation` (`{appointments}`) + `GET api.addDoctor` (array) with a single failure box + Retry, then re-dispatches `setAllappointments`/`setAllDoctor` so the home tiles stay correct. The doctors fetch deliberately does **not** reuse `fetchDoctors()` (`src/components/ApiService/ConsultationApiService.js`) because that helper swallows its error and could not feed the failure box.
- Status update: `PUT api.bookConsultation` with `{appointmentId, selectedStatus}`; on success the row is replaced in local state *and* in the store (the admin no longer has to reload to see the new chip), on failure an error note is shown.
- Files: `ConsultationBooked.js` (page shell: hero, tiles, cards), `BookingsTable.js` + `BookingRow.js` (new - 6 columns: Patient/Type/Appointment time/Symptoms/Status/Update status, search + `PanelPagination` 8/page), `DoctorList/DoctorsList.js` + `DoctorList/DocItemCards.js` (rewritten - Doctor/Area of expertise/Bookings/Actions, `Map`-grouped appointments, "View bookings" dialog reusing `SuperAdminModel`).
- `src/components/superAdminComponent/common/DoctorsTable.js` was **deleted**: this page was its only consumer. `common/AppointmentTable.js` (+ `RecentAppointment/Appointments.js` + `AppointmentItemCards.js`) is untouched because the earning pages and the LabTest booked page still render it.
- `css/ConsultationBooked.module.css` is **shared with the LabTest booked page** (`LabTestBooked.js` imports `bookingContainer`/`circle`/`circleText`) - the legacy block at the top of that file must stay until that page is redesigned too. Its new classes are appended below it.
- Traps worth remembering: `/superAdmin/*` panels render **client-side only** (the dev-server HTML is just the preloader overlay), so a `curl` can only prove the module graph compiles - a real render check needs Playwright with `**/api/auth/session**` stubbed, the APIs stubbed, and clicks dispatched through the DOM (`el.click()` via `evaluate`) while the preloader overlay is still fading.
- Pagination (follow-up): the two tables now render a folder-local `PanelPagination.js` instead of the shared `CustomPagination` (`src/helper.js`), which is a react-bootstrap `<Pagination>` and therefore picked up the *blue* `.page-link` pill (`#5496ff`, `0 8px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.15)`) from `public/css/style.css` - the only blue on the page. The new bar mirrors `/superAdmin/customerQuery` (`CustomerQueryComp` + `css/CustomerQueryComp.module.css`): `‹ Prev` / page numbers / `Next ›` / "Page x of y", centered under a 1px divider, green `#3b5f1d` active button on white text, `:focus-visible` ring, disabled Prev/Next at the ends. Same props as the helper (`currentPage`/`totalItems`/`itemsPerPage`/`onPageChange`) and still renders nothing for a single page, so the swap was mechanical (`itemsPerPage` stays 8 / 7); past 7 pages the middle collapses to `1 2 … 10` (the `"gap-<n>"` sentinel is both the marker and the React key). `CustomPagination` itself is untouched - 8 other panel pages still render it.
- Verified (pagination): `npx next lint` = 0 errors/0 warnings from these files; Playwright (throwaway `scripts/tmp-verify-pagination.mjs`, since deleted) with the session + both APIs stubbed at 80 bookings / 20 doctors = **35/35 checks** on desktop 1440 and mobile 390: `Page 1 of 10`, the `1 2 … 10` window, green active pill (no blue anywhere), `Next ›`/`‹ Prev` actually paging with different rows, disabled Prev on page 1 and disabled Next on page 10, doctors bar at `Page 1 of 3` with 7 rows/page, the consultations bar vanishing when a search leaves one page, and no bar overflow at 390px. The only console output left is pre-existing page noise (a `RightSideMenu` render warning + the next/head + `loader.gif` LCP bundle warnings), which a control run with 3 rows - no pagination rendered at all - reproduces identically.

- Follow-up (date filter + closed/payment columns): the page grew a **page-wide date filter** - `selectedDate` (`""` = all dates, the default) plus `Today` / `All dates` buttons and an "N of M bookings on 04 Oct 2026" note, all in one bar (`dateBar`) under the hero. `<input type="date">` already yields `YYYY-MM-DD`, which is exactly what `istDayKey()` prints, so the day is compared directly (never `toISOString().slice(0,10)` - that is the UTC day, and 18:45Z belongs to the *next* IST day). One `datedAppointments` memo (tiles, Consultations table **and** the per-doctor counts all read it) keeps the whole page on one day; `formatIstDate` prints the label. Rows with a missing/unparseable `appointmentTime` only show under "All dates".
- 4th filter tile **"Consultation closed"**: defined as *the prescription has been shared with the patient*, i.e. `prescriptionUrl` is set (223 rows live: `prescriptionUrl` 20, Payments PAID 24, both 0 - the two "done" buckets do not overlap today). It is a UI-only sentinel `CLOSED_FILTER = "CLOSED"` (never written to the DB, deliberately not part of `appointment_status`), and each closed row prints "Prescription shared" under its status chip.
- `GET api/bookConsultation` now `.populate("paymentId", "status amount paidAt method orderId").lean()` and adds **derived** `paymentStatus` / `hasPrescription` / `isClosed` to every appointment (computed per response, never stored - `PUT` still writes only `status`; `?doctorId=` unchanged). Additive for the existing `paymentId` readers (`common/ViewAppointment.js`, `RecentAppointment/*`), which read it as an object and just showed `N/A` before. **Trap:** a `populate` needs the referenced model registered on the connection, so the route side-effect-imports `../../src/models/paymentSchema`; without it mongoose throws `MissingSchemaError` and the GET 500s with a useless `undefined` in the log (the handler only logs `error.status`).
- `ConsultationBooked/consultationFlags.js` (new) owns the derived logic for both tables: `isClosed` / `hasPrescription` / `isPaid` / `paymentStatusOf` (each falls back to recomputing from the document, so a row from the redux store or sessionStorage still works) and `paymentBadge()` -> `{label, tone}`: `PAID` "Paid" · `PAYMENT_PENDING`/`INITIATED` "Payment pending" · `FAILED` "Payment failed" · `CANCELLED` "Payment cancelled" · `REFUND_PENDING`/`REFUNDED` "Refund pending"/"Refunded" · no `paymentId` "No payment record"; tone maps to `.paymentPaid`/`.paymentPending`/`.paymentFailed`/`.paymentRefund`/`.paymentNone`.
- Columns (both the table and the doctor dialog): **Patient name & ID** (8-char booking id, full value in the `title`) · **Consultation type** · **Appointment date & time** · **Doctor** (`doctorDisplayName`) · **Department** (`doctor.expertise`, else `serviceOffered.join(", ")`, else "Not recorded") · **Payment status** · **Symptoms** · **Consultation status** · **Update status**. Doctor/department come from one `doctorsById` `Map` built from the roster that is already fetched, and an unresolved `doctorId` prints "Doctor not available". The search box now also matches doctor, department and the payment label; the 9-column table sets `.table` `min-width: 1040px` (it still scrolls inside `.tableWrap`).
- Verified (date filter + columns): `npx next lint` 0 errors/warnings from the touched files; live `curl` on `GET /api/bookConsultation` = 223 appointments, `paymentStatus: "PAID"` 24, `isClosed` 20, populated `paymentId` 45 (keys present on every row); throwaway Playwright probe (temp spec + temp config, both deleted) **8/8** at desktop 1440 and mobile 390 with the session + both APIs stubbed - 4 tiles, 9 renamed headers, short id, doctor/department cells, the four payment labels, "Prescription shared", search over the new columns, the date filter driving tiles + caption + doctor dialog, and the IST boundary (18:45Z on 10-04 only appearing under 10-05). **Playwright trap:** a single `*` in a route glob does not match `/`, and these endpoints are called with a trailing slash (`api.bookConsultation === "/api/bookConsultation/"`), so stubs must use `**/api/bookConsultation**` - `**/api/bookConsultation*` silently lets the *real* API through (the page then shows 223 rows and every fixture assertion fails).
- **Bug fixed (status dropdown showed the wrong status):** `BookingRow.js`'s `STATUS_OPTIONS` listed only PENDING/CONFIRMED/RESCHEDULED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED, but every freshly booked consultation is stored as `OPEN` (`pages/api/helper.js` writes `appointment_status.open`; live data = 147 OPEN · 33 PENDING · 24 CONFIRMED · 19 COMPLETED). A `<select>` whose `value` matches no `<option>` silently falls back to its first option, so 147 rows showed a **PENDING** dropdown beside an **OPEN** badge and the stored value could not be re-selected. `appointment_status.open` now leads `STATUS_OPTIONS` and maps to `.badgePending` — the same colour the doctor panel gives OPEN (`registerDocComponent/homepage/appointmentStatus.js`).
- **Bug fixed (table overflowed its card):** the nine-column Consultations table measured 1336px inside a 1102px card, so "Consultation status" / "Update status" were clipped behind a horizontal scroll at *every* desktop width — the `min-width: 1040px` intent was defeated by `white-space: nowrap` headers plus long cell content. `.th` lost `nowrap` (+ `padding: 8px 10px`) so two-word headers wrap, `.td` padding went 12px -> 10px, and `.name`/`.nameBtn` gained `overflow-wrap: anywhere` so a long unbreakable patient name (test data: `livebookingwhatsapptest`) cannot stretch the table. Result: table 1102px == wrap width at >=1280 (no scroll, all nine columns visible); <=1024 still scrolls inside the card, as designed.
- Not a page bug: the `RightSideMenu` / `MyApp` "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component" console error is **app-wide** (reproduces on `/superAdmin/homepage`, `/superAdmin/labTestBooked`, `/superAdmin/customerQuery`, `/superAdmin/addDoctor`), so it was left alone.
- Verified (fixes): `npx next lint` 0 errors/warnings; Playwright (throwaway `scripts/tmp-cb-check.mjs`, since deleted) at 1600/1440/1366/1280/1024/390 = 9 columns, table fits (no `tableWrap` scroll at >=1280), badge->select now `OPEN->OPEN`, `COMPLETED->COMPLETED`, and 0 page errors.



### Super-admin `/superAdmin/consultationBooked` - date range, stacked date/time, widened table, dual status update

- **Date filter is now a range.** `ConsultationBooked.js` replaced the single `selectedDate` with `fromDate`/`toDate` (`#consultationFromDate` / `#consultationToDate`, `max`/`min` cross-clamped). Each is a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` from the native picker, i.e. exactly what `istDayKey()` prints, so the filter is an inclusive *string* compare with no timezone maths; `""` on either end leaves that side open, both `""` = every date, and a reversed range is read as the span it covers (`from > to` is swapped once, and the same swap feeds the label, so it can never print a start later than its end). A single day (both ends equal, e.g. after **Today**) prints once - not `05 Oct 2026 - 05 Oct 2026`. Every count on the page (4 tiles, both tables, the per-doctor dialog) still reads the one `datedAppointments` memo, and rows whose `appointmentTime` is missing only appear under "All dates". `dateLabel` now reads `from X` / `up to Y` / `X - Y`.
- **Chart cell stacks date over time.** `BookingRow` + `DoctorList/DoctorsList` print `formatIstDate()` above `extractTime()` in `.cellStack` (`.dateLine` bold, `.timeLine` muted), replacing the single `nowrap` `formatData()` string (~200px of min-content, the widest thing in the table). Do **not** use `extractDate()` for this - it reads local `getDate()/getMonth()`, while every other value on the page is IST-pinned.
- **Widths are pinned by `<colgroup>`, not by content.** `BookingsTable` declares 9 columns `[198, 61, 110, 116, 119, 114, 98, 137, 149]` = **1102px** = `.table`'s `min-width`, so at >=1280 the card (1180px page - 32px page padding - 44px card padding - 2px card border = 1102) and the table match exactly and the wrap never scrolls. For that to hold, *no cell may want more than its column*: `.td`/`.th` carry `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (min-content ~= 1 character, max-content untouched, so a word still stays whole whenever it fits) - without it the browser grows the table instead (`min-content > width` beats the colgroup, and auto layout then ignores it entirely, which is how the previous 9-column overflow happened). Headers were shortened (`Type`, `Date & time`, `Status`) so every header word fits its column, and the payment chip (`styles.paymentChip { white-space: normal }`) wraps to two lines instead of forcing that column from 114px to 148px.

- Widths were **measured, not guessed**: the probe fixture carries a worst-case row (`RESCHEDULED` badge + "Prescription shared" tag + `Gastroenterology` department + `Video consultation` type + an unbreakable 33-char name) and the geometry assertion reads back each `<col>`/`<th>` width plus an injected span measuring every header's widest word against its content box. The real 223-row API confirms 1102 == 1102 at 1440/1280, the wrap still scrolls at 1024 (by design), and there is no page-level overflow at 390.
- **"Update status" now updates both statuses.** The last cell holds two stacked selects (ids `payment-status-<id>` above `status-<id>`) over one Update button, and only the field(s) that actually changed travel in the PUT (a payment-less booking is never rejected for a payment it did not touch). The payment select's option **value** is the raw enum and its **label** comes from `PAYMENT_STATUS_LABELS` (`PAID -> "Paid"`, `PAYMENT_PENDING -> "Pending"`, `INITIATED -> "Initiated"`, ...) because `PAYMENT_PENDING`/`INITIATED` share the "Payment pending" chip copy and the raw enum does not fit the 129px select; a stored value outside the list is prepended with its raw label so the select and the chip above it can never disagree. A booking with no linked `Payment` shows a leading `""` option (`No payment`) instead.
- **`pages/api/bookConsultation.js` PUT was missing `await dbConnect()`** (the GET had it) - a latent cold-start "buffering timed out" bug, now fixed. PUT also accepts optional `selectedStatus` + `selectedPaymentStatus`, enum-checks both, and is **atomic**: the linked Payment is resolved and rejected *first*, so a payment change on an appointment with no Payment returns 400 `No payment record for this appointment` with nothing written (no half-applied consultation status). `paymentSchema.status` is updated (plus `paidAt` the first time it turns `PAID`) and the response is `{ message, status, paymentStatus }`. Widening the contract is safe: `ConsultationBooked.js` is the only caller of this PUT (verified).
- Client behaviour worth knowing before "fixing" it: the handler writes **both** fields into local state + redux, and on failure surfaces the API's own message in the existing note while the two selects keep the admin's draft (the row's badge/chip still show the *stored* values, so the change is visibly unsaved and the payment select can be corrected and retried).
- Verified: `npx next lint` -> 0 errors/warnings from the touched files; throwaway Playwright probe (temp spec + temp config, both deleted) **2/2** - a 5-row stubbed fixture (from-only / to-only / both / reversed / Today, stacked-line geometry via `getBoundingClientRect`, name on one line via `getClientRects().length === 1`, both selects enabled, PUT bodies `{appointmentId, selectedStatus}` vs both fields, the 400 no-payment path leaving the stored badge/chip untouched, plus the geometry block) and a real-API test at 1440/1280/1024 (223 rows, 2 selects per visible row, no wrap scroll >=1150, 0 page errors).
- Probing trap (on top of the `**/api/bookConsultation**` glob): a row locator must be scoped - `table tbody tr` also matches the **Doctors** table rendered below (`DoctorsList`), so a 3-booking fixture counts 4 rows. Use `table:has(caption) tbody tr` (only the Consultations table has a `<caption>`).


## Free follow-up policy (48 hours, same/related problem only)

- The condition "free follow-up is available only within 48 hours of your consultation and only for the same or a related problem" is stated in three places, all hardcoded copy: `/terms-of-service` (`src/components/Terms/TermsPage.js`, paragraph at the end of §4 "Consultations and Prescriptions"), `/privacy-policy` (`src/components/Terms/PrivacyPolicy.js`, §2 "How We Use Information") and the super-admin invoice `TERMS & CONDITIONS` list (`generateInvoiceImage.js`, 4th `<li>`; safe to extend because html2canvas captures full height and the jsPDF page is sized from the canvas).
- The booking form's consent block deliberately carries **no** follow-up note - it was added under the same request and removed again on the next one, and the `af.followUpNote` keys were deleted from `src/i18n/translations.js` with it. Only the two policy pages and the invoice carry the wording in prose.
- FAQ answer: "Is the follow-up consultation free?" lives in `data/faqs.js` inside the **General Questions** group, as the **2nd** question of that group - it is the first question most visitors read after "How do I book..." and it is the page's first group, so nothing has to be expanded or scrolled to spot it. `data/faqs.js` stays the single source of truth for the copy (visible Q&A and schema cannot drift) and the appointment page FAQ carries it bilingually as its 4th item (`src/components/Appointment/common/FAQComponent.js` -> `faq.q4`/`faq.a4` in `src/i18n/translations.js`).
- It sits in General Questions **instead of** the `Online & In-Clinic Doctor Consultation` group: `/faqs` renders every group, so a copy in both would print the same question twice on the page (and twice in the FAQPage schema). The price of that choice is that the `getFaqsForTopic("consultation")` FAQ shown on consultation topic pages / `/service-details?Service=consultation` keeps its original 5 questions and no longer lists the free-follow-up one - the promise still reaches readers through `/faqs` and the appointment page.
- Probing trap: `/faqs` is SSG and its **body is client-rendered** - the served HTML is just the preloader (`<div id="__next"><div class="Preloader_overlay__...`), so a `curl`/body grep finds **only** the `<head>` JSON-LD, never the visible accordions ("General Questions" etc. are absent from the HTML). Grep the HTML for the schema and use Playwright for the visible list. The accordion itself is Bootstrap `collapse` with **one open card per group** (first card of each group), and collapsed answers are absent from `innerText` - expand first (`a[data-toggle="collapse"]`) and read the enclosing `.card`; the appointment page equivalent is MUI (`.MuiAccordionSummary-root`).
- Verified on :3000 with a throwaway probe (deleted): `/faqs` renders 72 cards in 20 groups with the question appearing **exactly once**, at page index **1** (= "1. General Questions", between "How do I book a doctor consultation or any other service?" and "What are your working hours?"), still expandable to the full answer, matching the head FAQPage JSON-LD (72 questions, index 1); `/service-details?name=Doctor Consultation&Service=consultation` returns 200 with the consultation-group FAQ and no free-follow-up question; the appointment FAQ renders 4 items with the follow-up answer in EN and, with `localStorage.app_lang = "hi"`, the Hindi question + answer; no page errors; `npx next lint` -> 0 errors.

## Deploy failure policy (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) — fail safe, roll back only on request

- **A failed run changes nothing.** The old workflow was broken by design: `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` → `mv .next .next.prev` → `npm run build` all ran **before** the rollback could help, and the only rollback trigger was `trap rollback ERR`. A dropped ssh transport (`client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, exit 255) kills the remote shell with `SIGHUP`, which an `ERR` trap never sees — so on 2026-10-10 a staging deploy died inside "Creating an optimized production build…", left `3c610db` checked out with a half-written `.next`, never reloaded PM2, and the site stayed down on both domains.
- The deploy now **builds into a side directory** (`NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-next npm run build`, wired through `distDir: process.env.NEXT_DIST_DIR || '.next'` in `next.config.js`; PM2 leaves the var unset, so the running app still reads plain `.next`). The live `.next` and PM2 are untouched until `BUILD_ID` exists in `.next-next`; only then does the switch happen (`rm -rf .next.prev` → `mv .next .next.prev` → `mv .next-next .next` → `pm2 reload`). Anything failing before that prints `✗ DEPLOY FAILED - nothing on the VPS was switched` and exits **without touching the tree, the build or PM2** (the checkout stays on the new commit on purpose, so a retry is cheap).
- **No automatic rollback.** `rollback()`/`trap rollback ERR` are gone; `trap … HUP INT TERM` only reports and exits 130. Reverting is an explicit action: re-run the workflow with `mode=rollback` (`workflow_dispatch` input), which moves `.next` → `.next.broken`, restores `.next.prev`, reloads PM2 and deletes `.next.broken`.
- `.next.prev` is therefore **never deleted on success** any more — it is the artifact `mode=rollback` restores (each successful deploy replaces it). `.next-next` is wiped before every build, and all three dirs are gitignored.
- The post-deploy health check is **report only** (a failure turns the run red and prints the revert one-liner). When `VPS_HEALTH_URL_*` is unset it falls back to a PM2 `online` check instead of silently skipping.
- ssh hardening on the deploy step: `-o ConnectTimeout=15 -o ServerAliveInterval=15 -o ServerAliveCountMax=8 -o TCPKeepAlive=yes` (the old command had no keepalive at all), and `timeout-minutes` 25 → 45 so a job timeout cannot decapitate a silent build.
- Known trade-off of "keep the checkout on the new commit": after a failed run the tree is at the new commit while the live build is the old one. Safe as long as `server.js` is unchanged; the app keeps serving the old `.next` through a PM2 restart too.



## Slots / doctor working hours (2026-10-10) — why production had zero slots

- Two env files are tracked in git and differ in **database**: `./.env` → `IATRIC_test` (dev), `./.env.production` → `IATRIC` (production). Scripts default to `.env`; the slot script takes `--env=production`.
- `pages/api/lib/cron-jobs.js` is the only code that inserts into `slots`, and it **skips any doctor with a null `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime`** (`console.warn`, easy to miss). Both production doctors had them null, so `slots` stayed empty while everything looked healthy. The fields are optional in `src/models/doctorModel.js`; the admin *edit* PUT does not persist them either (only Add Doctor POST and the approved `doctorUpdateReq` PUT can).
- Time convention for the two window fields: the value is the **UTC instant of the intended IST wall time** — 07:00–22:00 IST is stored as `01:30Z`–`16:30Z`. The generator reads the UTC clock (`getUTCHours`), while the doctor profile renders the browser clock (`convertDateIntoTime` in `src/helper.js` uses `getHours()`), so an IST browser shows 07:00–22:00 for those values.
- `npm run db:set-slot-windows` (dry run) / `npm run db:set-slot-windows:apply` → `scripts/setDoctorSlotWindows.js`, which fills the window **only where it is missing** (defaults 07:00–22:00 `+05:30`, overridable with `--start/--end/--offset`).
- Generate slots on demand with `curl -X POST https://healthpath.co.in/api/lib/runCronJob` (takes ~3 min; it generated Oct 11–16, 45 slots/day/doctor = 540 rows). **`server.js` nightly cron still POSTs to `/api/lib/cron-jobs`** — a task module with no `res.*`, so that call hangs, the log always says "Slot generation failed", and there is no boot catch-up. The correct endpoint is `/api/lib/runCronJob` (what the super-admin HeroBand button already uses).
- Appointment UI date convention: `fetchSlot` windows its query on the **UTC day** of the `date` it is given, so the picked day must be sent as noon UTC (`ManageSlotsModal` already does `selectedDate + "T12:00:00Z"`; `AppointmentPage.todayAtNoonUTC` and `Appointmentform.handleDateChange` now do the same). A local-midnight `Date` resolved to the *previous* UTC day for IST users.

## Consultation recording (meeting room)

- **Where:** the meeting room `src/components/MeetingRoom/MeetingRoom.js` drives everything through the hook `src/components/MeetingRoom/useConsultationRecorder.js`. The room previously had an `isRecording` boolean and a Record button that only toggled it; the boolean is now owned by the hook.
- **What is captured:** a single **mixed** file — both participants' video composited onto a 1280×720 canvas (`canvas.captureStream`) and both audio tracks summed with the Web Audio API (`createMediaStreamSource` → `createMediaStreamDestination`), fed to one `MediaRecorder` (vp9/vp8+opus WebM, `video/mp4` fallback for Safari; `audio/webm` for audio-only consultations). The peer's audio is folded into the live mix when they connect mid-call (`connectAudio` uses a `WeakSet` so a stream is never double-connected).
- **Who records / when:** **doctor's room only**, auto-started the moment the call is `active` and local media is ready (`enabled = isDoctor && meetingState === "active" && localMediaReady`), and stopped (which finalises + uploads) when the call ends or the room unmounts. The doctor's browser holds the local + remote streams, so one recording captures everyone; recording from both rooms would mean two uploads racing for the same `recordingURL` field. The patient's room never records (so it shows no recording UI). The Record button is doctor-only now, as a manual stop/restart.
- **Upload + persistence:** the blob goes straight from the browser to Firebase Storage at `images/consultationRecording/meeting=<meetingId>_<timestamp>.<ext>` (`consultation_recording_folder` in `src/constant.js`) via `src/services/consultationRecording.js` (`uploadBytes`/`getDownloadURL`, dynamically imported so the meeting-room bundle does not carry the Firebase SDK). The resulting URL is POSTed to the new route `pages/api/recording.js` (`api.recordingCall`), which writes `Appointment.recordingURL` — the schema field added by this feature (default `""`). The doctor panel and super-admin panel only *read* that field.
- **Display:** doctor — `homepage/DashboardSecond/AppointmentTable.js` (a "Recording" row action) and `ViewAllAppointmentComp.js` (a "Recording" column); super-admin — `common/ViewAppointment.js` ("Consultation Recording" row on the details page) and `ConsultationBooked/BookingRow.js` (a "▶ Recording" link under the status badge, class `.recordingLink`). Lists refetch from `GET /api/bookConsultation`, which spreads the appointment document, so `recordingURL` travels with it with no API change.
- **Infra note:** the client upload needs the Firebase Storage rules to permit writes under `images/consultationRecording/**` (or `production_img/**` in production) exactly as they already permit `images/prescription/**` — the prescription flow is the working precedent. No storage rules file lives in the repo (console-managed), and no server/Firebase Admin path is involved. Verified with `npx next lint` (0 errors) and `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-verify npx next build` (route `/api/recording` emitted; temp dir deleted).
- **CI trap:** Playwright's WebKit build on Linux has no usable `MediaRecorder`/`canvas.captureStream`, so the doctor's auto-recording assertions (`tests/e2e/meeting-url.spec.ts` › `doctor: the record control mirrors the automatic consultation recording`) failed on **all four WebKit projects** of a GitHub Actions run while Chromium, Firefox and macOS WebKit passed (Firefox uses the *same* synthetic stream from `installMeetingMedia()`, so the media helper is not at fault; retries never helped ⇒ deterministic, engine-level, exactly like the `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream` trap above). `tests/e2e/helpers/meeting-room.ts` now exposes `recordingCapabilities(page)` (raw facts: `MediaRecorder` / `canvas.captureStream` / Web Audio / encodable containers, mirroring `pickMimeType()`'s candidate lists) and `supportsRecording(page)`, which the test uses to `test.skip(...)` **on the browser that cannot record** instead of failing it — capable browsers keep the strict assertions, and the probe is attached to the report so a future regression says *what* is missing rather than just `Expected: 0, Received: 1`.
- **Not done (flag if asked):** the patient is not *told* they are being recorded (would need a socket `recording-start`/`-stop` relay so the non-recording room can show a badge), and the ended-call screen does not surface the upload progress — the header badge does while the call is live.
